intelligence.title: Payments the Simple Way — Paste a Link, We Track the Rest
intelligence.ingest_note: Filed same-push complete by Naya Resolve Narzan on 2026-11-04 from Shawn Vibert's relayed 2026-11-03 session — a ruling he stated and the relaying seat did not note; filed here so it is in the system and he never has to repeat it.
intelligence.essence: Functionality first, payments after — and when payments come on, they come on simply. There is no heavy integration to build: the membership owner pastes their own PayPal link or Stripe link into their settings — boom — members pay through it, and the system tracks who paid. PayPal and Stripe do the same job. Shawn already has PayPal hooked up, so PayPal is the first rail. The money rail belongs to the owner's own account; NayaNET never has to touch a card.
intelligence.human_view: If you run a membership, you should not need a developer and three weeks to take money. You take the payment link from the PayPal or Stripe account you already have, paste it into your membership's settings, and you are in business. Your members click, pay, and the system remembers who has paid and who has not. Everything else — the content, the gating, the member experience — is built and working before payments even enter the picture.
intelligence.simple_view: It is like putting your own lemonade money jar on the stand. You do not need the town to build you a bank. You bring your jar, people drop their coins in, and the list on the clipboard says who paid. Simple.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it works the way a church bake sale always worked: the money goes into your own tin, not somebody else's machine. You paste in your PayPal or Stripe link — the one from the account you already trust — and the system politely keeps the list of who has paid. No card numbers ever pass through our hands, dear, and that is exactly how it should be.
intelligence.naya_view: I never block working functionality on a payment integration — memberships, gating, scheduling and sync all ship and prove themselves first. When payments activate, my job is a settings field for the owner's own payment link and an honest paid/unpaid record per member. I do not build checkout machinery the owner's own PayPal or Stripe already provides, and I never store card data. This ruling supersedes any 'create a Stripe account and payment links first' checklist — including the one in the 2026-11-03 gap-closer report Shawn relayed: that ask is retired.
intelligence.ai_view: Every week spent integrating a payment processor is a week the membership system is not in citizens' hands. The paste-a-link model removes the entire integration project and replaces it with a field and a list — and it puts the money where it belongs: directly between the member and the owner, in the owner's own account, from the first sale. Simplicity here is not a shortcut; it is the architecture.

machine_view.title: Payments the Simple Way — Paste a Link, We Track the Rest
machine_view.machine_section: Owner setting: payment_link (a PayPal or Stripe payment URL) on the membership/page. Member flow: member pays at the owner's link → system tracks paid state per member (paid / not paid) for gating. No card data touches NayaNET at any point. Rails are equivalent by ruling; PayPal is first (Shawn's existing account). This citizen-membership rail is separate from the platform's own money contract (SN-1905 tiers + Ambassador 50% paid Wednesdays), which stands unchanged.
